summary: Bank of England Working Paper No. 179 (published 7 March 2003) by Jennifer V Greenslade, Richard G Pierse and Jumana Saleheen applies the Kalman filter to UK Phillips-curve models to estimate the NAIRU from 1973 to 2000. The estimates suggest the NAIRU peaked around the mid-1980s and fell afterwards, partly due to labour market structural changes and temporary effects of real import and oil prices. The authors note uncertainty in the estimates but find that unemployment was below the NAIRU for much of the second half of the 1990s across a variety of models.
one_line: Bank of England working paper using Kalman filter Phillips-curve models to estimate the UK's NAIRU from 1973 to 2000.
key_facts: Bank of England Working Paper No. 179 is titled 'A Kalman filter approach to estimating the UK NAIRU'.
The paper was published on 07 March 2003.
The authors are Jennifer V Greenslade, Richard G Pierse and Jumana Saleheen.
The Kalman filter method is applied to UK Phillips-curve models.
NAIRU estimates are derived for the period from 1973 to 2000.
The resulting profiles suggest the NAIRU peaked around the mid-1980s and fell back thereafter.
Structural changes in the labour market have reduced inflationary pressure from that source.
Temporary effects from real import prices and real oil prices were an important additional downward influence on inflation in the latter half of the 1990s.
Some uncertainties around the NAIRU estimates are shown in the paper.
A variety of models suggest that unemployment was below the NAIRU for much of the second half of the 1990s.
The working papers series aims to set out research in progress by Bank of England staff, encouraging comments and debate.
